items.title: Show HN: Pantry an open source scanner that checks what your coding agents run
items.desc: title: "Pantry: free vulnerability scanner for macOS, Linux and Windows" description: "Pantry finds the vulnerabilities that actually apply to your machine and fixes what it safely can. Free and open source, written in Rust. No telemetry, no AI." url: "https://waffuru.ai/products/pantry" language: "en" Free · Open source · macOS, Linux and Windows Useful AI starts with security. Before agents run on your machines, the machines have to be safe. Pantry checks everything installed on your Mac or Linux machine, and every repo on it, against open vulnerability and malware data. It reports only what actually applies, names the version that fixes it, and applies the fixes it safely can. [Secure your system](https://waffuru.ai/products/pantryinstall) [Learn more](https://waffuru.ai/blog/introducingpantry) [View the source on GitHub](https://github.com/waffuruai/pantry) Runs on macOS Windows Linux Ubuntu Debian Fedora Arch Omarchy On Windows, Pantry checks your repos and a first few installed programs; full machine checks are coming. [Tell us what you need](mailto:hello@waffuru.ai?subject=Pantry%20on%20Windows) Free · open source Free Pantry costs nothing, and its MITlicensed source code is open to everyone. Local Scans run on your machine. Only package names and versions ever leave it. Fast Later scans take seconds, because Pantry checks only what changed, from a cache on your disk. Attacks don’t wait for a CVE. Agents now read your repos, run your tools and hold your keys. Two attacks from November 2026 show what that puts at stake. Neither came with a CVE, so a CVE feed would not have been helpful. Bitdefender Labs · Nov 17, 2026 GitHub repos that hijack your AI coding agent Bitdefender found 22 GitHub repos that get AI coding assistants to run a hidden setup script, through AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, a Claude Code sessionstart hook, MCP configs and VS Code tasks. The script steals tokens, SSH keys and cloud credentials, then plants the same configs in the victim’s other repos. What Pantry checks Code a repo runs the moment it is opened (Claude Code and Gemini hooks, MCP servers kept in the repo, VS Code tasks on folder open), payloads decoded at run time and fed to eval, and every MCP server your agents start. [Read the report](https://www.bitdefender.com/enus/blog/labs/howaiagentsbecomenewtargetsingithubmalwarecampaign) Report URI · Nov 16, 2026 Malware on 178 organisations’ sites, through Optimizely An attacker added a loader to customers’ Optimizely Web project code. Pages at 178 organisations, some of the world’s largest brands among them, then swapped crypto addresses, skimmed cards, stole cookies and sent iPhones to exploit kits. What Pantry checks The payload lived in a vendor’s dashboard, out of reach of any scanner on your machine. Pantry flags the opening it used, thirdparty scripts your repos load without an integrity hash, and code shaped like the payload: strings decoded and fed to eval, clipboard address swaps and card data in the clear. [Read the report](https://blog.reporturi.com/worldslargestbrandsinfectedwithmalwareviaoptimizely/) Install. Scan. Cache. Fix. One small binary does the whole job on your machine. Only package names and versions ever leave it. 01 · Install Verified before it runs 02 · Scan Only what applies 03 · Cache Seconds, the second time 04 · Fix Fixes you can trust Pantry can read your whole home directory, so every release is signed, hashed and built reproducibly. packslip, GitHub or cosign checks the download before it ever runs. Pantry takes stock of your runtimes, packages, apps and every repo lockfile, then asks OSV.dev, CISA KEV and endoflife.date about those exact versions. Nothing you have not installed gets reported. Answers land in a SQLite database on your disk, along with a record of every run. A second scan the same day takes seconds, and you can search the advisories offline. Preview the plan, then let Pantry run the safe, userlevel updates and check again. Anything that needs sudo or a code change is printed for you or your agent to run. Play wpantry Install $ mise use g packslip:github.com/waffuruai/pantry verifies the signed packslip, then the binary’s digest$ wpantry versionwpantry 0.4.0 (rust, schema 1) 1. Signed release 2. Signature + SHA256 3. Your machine A download that fails either check is never installed. Example output from one machine. Yours will differ. Secure your system. Choose how much you want to check yourself. Every route verifies the release before anything runs. With the install script With mise Verify it yourself Other package managers Recommended With the install script Picks the build for your machine, checks it against SHA256SUMS, verifies its signature with packslip, the GitHub CLI or cosign, and installs it to ~/.local/bin. [Read the script first](https://github.com/waffuruai/pantry/blob/HEAD/rust/release/install.sh) With the install script Copy curl fsSL https://waffuru.ai/pantry/install.sh sh Then scan, see the plan, and write an HTML report. wpantry Copy wpantry scanwpantry fix dryrunwpantry report html Reports in every format. Read it in your terminal, share one offline HTML page, or hand JSON to your tools and agents. wpantry report turns the latest scan into any of them, without scanning again. HTML Terminal JSON JSON Lines CSV Markdown One offline page to read, share or print: what was checked, what applies, the exact fix for each, and a prompt to hand your coding agent. wpantry report html Pantry’s HTML report for an example project: three things to update, a prompt for a coding agent, and the findings for smallvec, lodash and requests. Example reports from one example project. Yours will differ. [See the whole report](https://waffuru.ai/img/pantry/reporthtml2560.jpg?v=a608300869) Verify everything on your computer. A pantry check covers what you have, what is past its date, what needs to be replaced and what someone has tampered with. Everything installed Runtimes and compilers (every version your version ma

items.title: Show HN: Riemann Hypothesis Proof for Learners
items.desc: description: The concepts that the proof needs, in the order that you need them, with the reason for each one and links to Math 2.0. title: What to learn first [Skip to the content](content) The Lean code claims a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. This site has not checked the claim yet. [See what is checked](/trust/). How to use this page The path has three stages. Stage 1 is enough to read [the proof in one page](/proof/) and to check its classical part yourself. Stage 2 is enough to understand the statement that does all the work. Stage 3 is the background of the large part of the Lean code. Each name links to its page in [Math 2.0](https://math2.tamnd.com), which has its own learning paths and exercises. Go through a stage in order. Skip a step when you know it. Stage 1\. The top of the proof At the end of this stage you can read the four steps at the top of the proof and check each one with pen and paper. 1. [Complex numbers](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/complexnumbersaspairsofreals/ "Complex numbers as pairs of reals in Math 2.0"). The zeros of ζ\\zeta are complex numbers s\=σ+its = \\sigma + it, and the Riemann Hypothesis is a claim about their real part σ\=Re⁡(s)\\sigma = \\operatorname{Re}(s). 2. [Holomorphic functions](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/holomorphicfunctiondefinition/ "Holomorphic function in Math 2.0"). The zeta function and the Lfunctions are holomorphic. A holomorphic function that is not zero has isolated zeros, so "the zeros of ζ\\zeta" is a set of points. 3. [Analytic continuation](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/analyticcontinuation/ "Analytic continuation in Math 2.0") and [meromorphic functions](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/meromorphicfunctiondefinition/ "Meromorphic function in Math 2.0"). The series ∑n−s\\sum n^{s} converges only for Re⁡(s)\1\\operatorname{Re}(s) 1. The function ζ\\zeta on all of ℂ\\mathbb{C} is its continuation. It has one pole, at s\=1s = 1, which is why the Lean statement excludes s\=1s = 1. 4. The [Gamma function](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/gammafunctiondefinition/ "Gamma function in Math 2.0") and its [reflection formula](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/reflectionformulaforthegammafunction/ "Reflection formula for the gamma function in Math 2.0"). The functional equation contains Γ(1−s)\\Gamma(1 s). The proof needs one fact about it: Γ\\Gamma has no zeros. 5. The [Riemann zeta function](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/riemannzetafunctiondefinition/ "Riemann zeta function in Math 2.0") and the [Euler product formula](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/eulerproductformula/ "Euler product formula in Math 2.0"). The Euler product shows that ζ(s)≠0\\zeta(s) \\neq 0 for Re⁡(s)\1\\operatorname{Re}(s) 1. It also shows why the zeros of ζ\\zeta carry information about the primes. 6. The [functional equation](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/functionalequationoftheriemannzetafunction/ "Functional equation of the Riemann zeta function in Math 2.0") of ζ\\zeta. It relates ζ(s)\\zeta(s) and ζ(1−s)\\zeta(1 s). Step 4 of the overview uses it to move a zero from the left of the line Re⁡(s)\=12\\operatorname{Re}(s) = \\tfrac12 to the right of it. 7. The [Riemann hypothesis](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/riemannhypothesis/ "Riemann hypothesis in Math 2.0"). Read the standard statement and compare it with the Lean statement on [the trust page](/trust/), question Q4. Stage 2\. The statement that does the work The Lean proof gets the Riemann Hypothesis from a statement about all Dirichlet Lfunctions at once. This stage explains that statement. 1. [Dirichlet characters](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/dirichletcharacterdefinition/ "Dirichlet character in Math 2.0"). A Dirichlet character modulo NN is a function χ\\chi on the integers that is periodic with period NN, multiplicative, and zero on the integers that share a factor with NN. The trivial character modulo 1 is the constant 1. 2. [Dirichlet Lfunctions](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/dirichletlfunctiondefinition/ "Dirichlet Lfunction in Math 2.0"). The function L(s,χ)\=∑χ(n)n−sL(s, \\chi) = \\sum \\chi(n) n^{s}, continued to all of ℂ\\mathbb{C}. For the trivial character modulo 1 it is ζ(s)\\zeta(s). This is how the proof gets from all characters to ζ\\zeta. 3. The [Gauss sum](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/gausssum/ "Gauss sum in Math 2.0"). It is the constant in the functional equation of L(s,χ)L(s, \\chi) for a primitive character. The theorem LFunction_eq_zero_re_of_isPrimitive of Main.lean uses that functional equation. 4. The [generalized Riemann hypothesis](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/generalizedriemannhypothesis/ "Generalized Riemann hypothesis in Math 2.0"). The statement EveryCharacter says that L(s,χ)≠0L(s, \\chi) \\neq 0 when Re⁡(s)\12\\operatorname{Re}(s) \\tfrac12, for each Dirichlet character, with the pole of ζ\\zeta as the only exception. That is the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet Lfunctions, in the form "no zeros to the right of the line". Stage 3\. The large part Below EveryCharacter the Lean code has more than 175,000 files. The [chapters](/proof/trunk/) explain its structure. The names of the Lean modules show the subjects that it uses: theta correspondences, unitary groups, automorphic forms, Galois representations and the local Langlands correspondence. Learn them in this order. Each group depends on the groups before it. Number fields and their characters. The large part works over number fields and their completions, not only over ℚ\\mathbb{Q}. [Number fields and algebraic integers](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/numberfieldsandalgebraicintegers/ "Number fields and algebraic integers in Math 2.0"), [quadratic fields](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/quadraticfielddefinition/ "Quadratic field in Math 2.0") and [ramification](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/ramificationdefinition/ "Ramification in Math 2.0"). [Local fields](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/localfield/ "Local field in Math 2.0") and [padic numbers](https://math2.tamnd.com/wiki/padicnumber/ "padic number in Math 2.0"). [Adeles and ideles]

[](/robinroy03/scenefinder/blob/main/docs/demo.gif) Install On macOS or Linux: curl fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robinroy03/scenefinder/main/install.sh sh On Windows, in PowerShell: irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robinroy03/scenefinder/main/install.ps1 iex Or let your AI agent do it. Paste this into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar: Install scenefinder on this computer. On macOS or Linux run: curl fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robinroy03/scenefinder/main/install.sh sh On Windows run this in PowerShell: irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/robinroy03/scenefinder/main/install.ps1 iex Then run scenefinder help to learn its commands, and from now on use it whenever I ask you to find or download a movie clip. Find $ scenefinder find "you shall not pass" m fellowship n 2 "you shall not pass": showing 2 of 4 clips MOVIE LEN LINE ID ── ────────────────────────────────── ───── ──────────────────────────── ───────────────────── 1 The Lord of the Rings: The… (2001) 0:07 You shall not pass youshallnotpasss8 2 The Lord of the Rings: The… (2001) 0:06 Gandalf: You shall not pass youshallnotpass 2 more: raise n, or try page 2 Several phrases can go in one call. m filters by movie title, max by length in seconds. Download $ scenefinder download gandalf=youshallnotpasss8 whyserious o clips STATUS FILE SIZE ────── ───────────────────── ──────── ok clips/gandalf.mp4 1.3 MB ok clips/whyserious.mp4 1.0 MB 2 downloaded, 0 already there, 0 failed Pass an ID from the find table, or NAME=ID to choose the file name. scenefinder help lists every flag. items.title: Show HN: Tab – a browser engine from scratch in Rust, with a demo to install
items.desc: description: Meet Tab: an independent Rust browser engine. Try the experimental Linux build, explore the real results, and see what still needs work. title: Tab: prealpha demo available image: https://gettab.dev/og.png A DIFFERENT KIND OF BROWSER Tab. A new browser. _Not a wrapper._ An independent web browser, built on its own engine in Rust. Familiar on the surface. Entirely new underneath. [Try the Linux demo ](demo) [See the test results](results) PrealphaLinux x8664Real engine. Real tests. [Take a look ](shot) 01 / THE EXPERIENCE The browser is the point. No Chromium, WebKit, or Gecko behind the curtain. Just Tab, rendering its own interface with the same engine it uses for the web. [A Tab window with one tab, New Tab, and kingmaker://newtab in the address bar. The start page shows the wordmark Tab. with its amber dot and the line ]() Tab's start page: plain HTML and CSS, drawn by Tab's own engine. A prerelease build of Tab on Linux. The screenshots are unedited, and the engine drawing these pages is the one the tests below measure. 02 / YOUR TURN Take it for a spin. The current experimental Linux build is ready for curious people to break it. One command installs Tab and opens a demo page. Tab is prealpha. It hasn't had a security audit, and plenty of real sites still break. Don't use it for banking, trading, or important logins. The first launch asks you to acknowledge this. While in prealpha, Tab counts its testers with one anonymous ping a day: a random ID, the version and your distro, never what you browse. TERMINAL / INSTALL TAB $ ./helloworldbutmakeitabrowser curl fsSL https://gettab.dev/install.sh sh s demo Copy command Current build 0.1.3107, built November 21, 2026. The script verifies SHA256 before installing. [Read the script first](/install.sh). Demo builds update themselves when a new build ships, and ask you to update after seven days. Found something broken? [Tell us on X](https://x.com/JacoblAmi1). 03 / THE RECEIPTS Tested against the web. No Chromium, WebKit or Gecko underneath: Tab's engine is new, testdriven and specremedied. It passes 1,886,506 of 1,917,339 tests across five upstream suites. Build 0.1.3096, measured November 20, 2026. Test262 100% 102,582 of 102,582 WPT testharness 98.59% 1,563,131 of 1,585,538 WPT rendering 91.19% 28,166 of 30,888 WPT remaining compatibility 90.45% 54,006 of 59,710 WebAssembly spec 100% 138,621 of 138,621 One developer architects the engine, builds the test pipelines, checks every result and calls out anything that doesn't hold up. AI agents, mostly Claude and GPT, write most of the code. The web's own test suites decide what's done. Pinned upstream catalogs under suite discovery/manifest rules; fixtures/support files excluded. See suite notes for catalog exclusions and identity caveats. NOT\_RUN, SKIP and harness errors remain in totals; only PASS counts as a pass. [Raw results](https://tabboard.pages.dev/board.json) 04 / THE HONEST PART No shortcuts on trust. About 70% of serious security bugs in Chrome are memorysafety bugs, by [Chromium's own count](https://www.chromium.org/Home/chromiumsecurity/memorysafety/). Writing Tab in Rust takes most of those off the table. The other 30% are logic: which site may read what, and when. That part is real work, built into the engine and tested side by side with Chromium with every request on the wire recorded. Here is where it stands. In place Sites can't read each other's data: crossorigin checks on fetch, XHR, redirects and preflights. Cookies follow HttpOnly and SameSite, across frames and redirects. Crossorigin images, fonts and frames can't leak through canvas, element capture or Location. One site's cached response is never served to another. Referrer Policy, Mixed Content blocking and Upgrade Insecure Requests. Subresource Integrity and Trusted Types. Still open No operatingsystem sandbox yet: the browser runs as a single process. Content Security Policy is only partly enforced. No independent security review yet. 245 security findings logged so far, each with its fix or the reason for a decision; 179 are fully fixed. 3 still open. Record as of November 12, 2026.
